BookALook · SuperAdmin · QA & test report

Money in Pocket & Analytics Dashboard

Release tested: commit 40b1050 (“report page”) and follow-up fixes · Report date: 06 November 2026

1. Summary

This release adds a “Money in pocket” figure to the SuperAdmin dashboard and replaces the Platform Reporting page with a full analytics dashboard (8 tabs, date-range and city/area filters, comparison with the previous period, CSV export). Every behaviour listed in section 4 is covered by an automated test that was run for this report; the results below are taken directly from the test run log, not written by hand.

39/39release test cases passed
371individual checks (assertions) in those cases
757tests passed in the full backend suite
2failures — both pre-date this release (section 5)

Frontend: TypeScript type-check and ESLint both clean on all changed files.

2. What was delivered

Money in pocket

What BookALook actually holds right now, and how much of it is its own once everything it owes has gone out. It is a running position since launch (the dashboard’s date range does not change it). Clicking the card shows every line behind the number.

Cash held = customer payments collected online (payment gateway only) + Subscription Plan payments approved (cash after coins) + commission dues paid in by salons − payouts already paid to salons − refunds already sent to customers − Razorpay fee (estimated, absorbed by BookALook) Money in pocket = Cash held − payouts calculated or approved but not yet paid − advances held for bookings no payout has settled yet − refunds still on their way to customers Shown but not counted until received: commission dues salons still owe, plan payments awaiting approval. Never counted: cash/UPI customers pay at the salon counter — that is the salon’s money from the start.

Analytics dashboard (Platform Reporting)

  • Overview — GMV, bookings, completed visits, average bill, customers, trading salons, online collections, BookALook earnings and take rate, payouts, refunds, cancellation and no-show rates; trends and highlights.
  • Money — online vs at-salon collections, refunds by status/reason/salon, payouts by status and billing model, commission and plan earnings, payment mix (advance / full / nothing online), Razorpay fee estimate, money-in-pocket breakdown.
  • Bookings — outcomes over time, app booking funnel, peak-time heatmap (weekday × hour), weekday averages, booking lead time, who cancels and why, reschedules.
  • Cities & areas — city and area tables (GMV, growth, share, average bill, reliability, customers, online money), demand against supply by area.
  • Salons & teams — full salon leaderboard (21 columns), fastest growing, most loyal, watch list, best rated, quiet salons, team utilisation per stylist.
  • Services — categories, services (revenue, growth, discounts, ₹ per chair-hour), combos, first-time offers, counter add-ons.
  • Customers — new vs returning, repeat rate, visit frequency, spend bands, 6-month cohort retention, gender mix, top customers with masked phone numbers, sign-ups and conversion.
  • Engagement — reviews and rating trend, lowest-rated salons, complaints and resolution time, WhatsApp campaigns and messages, notifications, reward coins.

3. How it was tested

  • Automated feature tests (39 cases, 371 checks) call the real API endpoints as a SuperAdmin against a test database, with data built for each case so every expected number is calculated by hand in advance.
  • Isolation — each test runs inside a database transaction that is rolled back, and builds its own city, salons and customers, so tests cannot affect each other or real data.
  • Full regression run — the whole backend suite (885 tests) was run to confirm nothing else broke.
  • Manual browser check — every tab, the city/area filters and the money-in-pocket breakdown were opened in the browser against a demo marketplace (screenshots in section 6).
  • Frontend static checks — TypeScript type-check and ESLint.
  • Production deployment — deployed to the live server (PostgreSQL); the new endpoints were confirmed responding after deployment.

Issue found and fixed during testing

A city or area filter value that is not a valid id (for example text that looks like SQL) would have caused a server error on the production database. The filters now validate the id and return a clear “invalid value” response (case “Filters: … refused with 422”). Also adjusted: when the previous period has no data, rate changes now show “new” instead of a misleading percentage-point jump.

7. Known limits

  • Razorpay fee is an estimate. Razorpay does not report its fee per payment to the platform, so it is estimated at 2.36% (2% + 18% GST) of Razorpay collections. The rate can be changed in configuration (RAZORPAY_FEE_PERCENT).
  • Money in pocket is a position, not a period. It is calculated since launch and does not follow the dashboard’s date range.
  • Money paid at the salon counter is never part of BookALook’s money; it is shown in reports for completeness only.
  • Team utilisation uses each stylist’s weekly working hours less approved full-day leave; part-day leave and salon closures are not deducted.
  • Ranges longer than two years are cut to the most recent two years to keep the dashboard fast.
